articles.title: Chilling grin of man accused of killing cop’s wife, daughter outside court after he gets 10 yrs in jail
articles.summary: Raipur: Kuldeep Sahu grins outside Surajpur court after getting 10 years for attempt to murder; convicted in 2024 cop’s wife-daughter murder, sentencing Oct 8.
articles.body: Raipur: “Achchha wala dikhaiyega, smile karte hue (Use a good pic, smiling one).” Moments after a Surajpur district fast-track court sentenced him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment for trying to mow down policemen with a car, Kuldeep Sahu, 28, walked out smiling at cameras and asked mediapersons to use his smiling picture.The video of Sahu grinning outside the courtroom circulated widely on social media, drawing attention not just to Monday’s sentence but also to the far graver case awaiting its final order: the 2024 murder of a head constable’s wife and minor daughter, in which Sahu and three others have been convicted. The court will pronounce the quantum of sentence in that case on Oct 8.Sahu was brought from Ambikapur central jail to Surajpur court under heavy security.The 10-year sentence relates to an incident from the night of Oct 13, 2024, when police were searching for Sahu after he attacked constable Ghanshyam Sonwani at Surajpur’s old bus stand by throwing boiling oil on him. During the ensuing police action, Sahu tried to run over a policeman with a car, according to the prosecution.The fast-track court convicted him in the attempt-to-murder case and sentenced him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment. Five other accused in that case were acquitted.The same night, the wife and minor daughter of a head constable posted in Surajpur were killed inside their rented house. Their bodies were later found around 5 km away.In that case, the court convicted Sahu along with Rinku alias Phool Singh, Chandrakant Chaudhary and Aryan Vishwakarma on charges including murder. Two other accused were acquitted. The court has reserved Oct 8 for sentencing.The prosecution case also includes sexual assault and Pocso Act charges linked to the double murder.Sahu had separately faced allegations of firing at a police team led by the then Bishrampur police station in-charge while fleeing near Latori, but he and another accused were acquitted in that case for lack of sufficient evidence.The double murder had triggered widespread outrage in Surajpur, with residents taking to the streets demanding strict punishment. Vehicles parked outside Sahu’s house and godown were torched during the unrest.Police records showed that Sahu had figured in more than two dozen criminal cases before the murders. articles.title: Jamia Millia Islamia suspends PhD scholar for 5 days over protest against hostel evictions
articles.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia suspends a PhD scholar for 5 days over alleged role in protest against women hostellers’ eviction notices; university cites rules.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia has suspended a PhD scholar for five days for allegedly participating in a protest gathering on Monday against the alleged “retaliatory” eviction notices served to several women hostellers who had staged a prolonged agitation over bugs found in mess food. The scholar has been barred from entering the campus during the suspension period.The show-cause notice, issued by the office of the chief proctor on Sept 28, said an unauthorised gathering was held at the central canteen at 5pm that day, disrupting the university’s routine functioning and affecting teaching, learning and research activities in nearby departments, laboratories and libraries. It accused the scholar of delivering a speech and “giving publicity to misleading accounts and rumours”, thereby inciting other students to breach discipline.The notice said his actions amounted to “gross misconduct” under various clauses of the university’s students’ discipline ordinance. He has been directed to explain by Oct 5 why a higher punishment should not be imposed.Speaking to TOI, the student said the protest was organised by women hostel residents against a recent alleged forced eviction, which they believed was retaliatory following their protests over food safety in the mess.Earlier, hostellers had alleged eviction notices were served on them for participating in protests against the mess food. The administration, however, had said the students did not meet the eligibility criteria and that hostel renewal was carried out every year on the basis of merit.Saima Saeed, chief public relations officer, Jamia Millia Islamia, said the university is not stopping anyone from exercising their right to protest. “The university has a designated site for protests, as per court orders, and if anyone violates these guidelines and disrupts the academic environment, the university is bound to take action. Secondly, Jamia follows a merit-based hostel allocation system. If a student does not meet the prescribed 55% marks criterion, we are only following the established procedure. articles.title: Military-grade drones worth Rs 1 crore seized at Delhi airport
articles.summary: Customs at Delhi IGI Airport seized professional-grade drones and parts worth Rs 1 crore from three passengers arriving from Hong Kong via Vietnam; DGCA registration required.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Three Indian passengers have been charged for attempting to smuggle drones and their parts worth Rs 1 crore. These passengers had arrived at IGI Airport on Sept 25 from Hong Kong via Vietnam.During Customs proceedings, the passengers were subjected to a baggage search, which resulted in the recovery of 10 autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 11 remote controllers of autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 10 adaptors, 10 USB chargers, 20 data cables, 40 remote controller joysticks and other parts. They also recovered one iPhone 18 Pro Max 512 GB.“Chartered engineer informed Customs officers that these are professional-grade drones with thermal imaging and laser range-finder and are military/defence grade UAV. They also require mandatory DGCA registration for each drone. The total market value was assessed at Rs 1 crore,” said a Customs official.The passengers told officials that the drones and their parts were brought from Hong Kong for a friend who owns them.“One passenger also stated that he intentionally smuggled these drones into India without declaration to the Customs authorities and without payment of applicable Customs duty,” said the official.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: ‘UP is my karmabhoomi, state will be starting point of my political journey’: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal
articles.summary: Ex-IAS officer Divya Mittal, 2013 UP cadre, enters politics independently in Uttar Pradesh, vows citizen-led platform, flags rural issues, road safety and jobs.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Tuesday announced her entry into politics but said she won’t join any party. Uttar Pradesh is my “karmabhoomi” and the state would be the starting point of my political journey, she said.Mittal, a 2013 batch UP cadre officer, resigned from the service earlier this month. Mittal said she would work directly with citizens and build an independent platform.She alleged that rumours circulated after her resignation were intended to discourage newcomers from entering public life. “I will not be deterred from raising public issues,” she said.In a video statement, Mittal said her administrative experience drove her decision. “I realised that many problems of the public do not get resolved even when approvals, funds and provisions are in place,” she said, adding, “There are people whose voices do not reach govt, and even when they do, their problems remain unheard.”“I want politics of intent, justice, concern and long-term thinking,” she said. “My objective is not just to replace political leaders. It is to change the way politics functions,” she added.She cited the example of a remote village where residents had sought a school offering education beyond Class V. Mittal said she approved the proposal, but construction had not begun years later. “It was not a question of funds or rules. There was a lack of intent,” she said.She also referred to a landless beneficiary who had official documents for an allotted plot but did not get its physical possession. “Inquiries found irregularities in the reports, and corrective action was taken. Yet the work did not move forward,” Mittal said, questioning what she described as “higher-level interference” in cases where people were legally entitled to relief.Mittal said she wanted to take up issues, including poor rural infrastructure, unsafe roads, examination paper leaks and employment concerns in the age of artificial intelligence. These, she said, needed greater public debate and attention from policymakers.She appealed to people from different walks of life, including teachers, farmers, students, doctors, labourers and lawyers, to join her effort. “Meaningful political change can come only through collective public participation,” she said.During her 13-year career, she also served as the district magistrate of Mirzapur and Deoria.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
articles.summary: Punjab govt tells Punjab and Haryana HC Gulzar Singh’s family hasn’t handed over the original suicide video/device; police rely on social media clips as SIT probes case.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. Multiple raids were also conducted at his residence, relatives houses and other possible locations.A petition was filed before the Punjab and Haryana high court seeking transfer of the investigation to the CBI or another independent agency, alleging that Gulzar Singh had faced intimidation and that his video statement contained allegations against certain persons.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: Meet Tejas: The rare blue-eyed white tiger who travelled 550 km from Gwalior to become Dehradun Zoo’s newest attraction; "The energetic young tiger immediately started exploring"
articles.summary: Dehradun Zoo just added a new attraction in the form of Tejas, a two-and-a-half-year-old white tiger.
articles.body: Dehradun Zoo just added a new attraction in the form of Tejas, a two-and-a-half-year-old white tiger. It gives wildlife enthusiasts another reason to visit the capital city. The little cub travelled nearly 550 km from Gwalior. He comes following an animal-exchange programme that saw the zoo’s approximately five-year-old Royal Bengal tiger, Bhola, move to Gwalior Zoological Park.For travellers planning a Dehradun visit, however, there is an important catch: Tejas will not be immediately visible to the public. After his journey of more than 14 hours, the young tiger has entered a period of quarantine and observation for about 20 days. So visitors will likely have to wait a month before he is put on display. During this period, his health, behaviour, feeding and adjustment to the new enclosure will be monitored.The blue-eyed Tejas As per reports, Tejas is particularly striking because of his white coat and dark stripes. He has beautiful blue eyes. But despite the unusual appearance, a white tiger is not a separate species or breed of tiger. The white coat results from an inherited colour variation; unlike an albino.As per TOI reports, Tejas was translocated under the administrative supervision of Neena Grewal, principal chief conservator of forests and chief wildlife warden. The transfer was overseen by Vaibhav Singh, divisional forest officer, Dehradun, with a 13-member specialised veterinary team accompanying the tiger. The team was led by Pradeep Mishra, senior veterinarian at Doon Zoo, along with SDO Abhishek Maithani.Sharing his observations on Tejas on the second day after his arrival, Mishra said, “With its white coat, crisp dark stripes and vivid blue eyes, he scanned everything in sight. He didn’t hesitate for a second; the energetic young tiger immediately started exploring, confidently strutting along the fence, sniffing the air and checking out every inch of his new home with bold curiosity.”Dehradun Zoo, a new stop for wildlife loversDehradun Zoo, formerly known as Malsi Deer Park, is located along Mussoorie Road at the foothills of the Shivalik range. The municipal administration describes it as a mini-zoological park developed with objectives that include ex-situ conservation, biodiversity conservation, wildlife education and rescue.The zoo is around 9–10 km from Dehradun's Clock Tower/city centre and lies on the route towards Mussoorie.The addition of Tejas also adds another layer to a city that already works as a gateway to several of Uttarakhand's best-known natural and hill destinations. The state tourism department describes Dehradun as a gateway to Mussoorie, Haridwar and Rishikesh, while also highlighting attractions such as the Forest Research Institute, Sahastradhara, Mindrolling Monastery and zoo.Other wildlife attractions nearbyTravellers interested in seeing wildlife in a natural setting can extend their trip to Rajaji National Park and Tiger Reserve, which spans parts of Dehradun, Haridwar and Pauri Garhwal districts. The reserve is known for its forest landscape and populations of elephants, tigers and leopards, besides a wide variety of birds and other wildlife.Rajaji can therefore complement a Dehradun itinerary for travellers who want to experience both wildlife conservation in a zoo setting and the biodiversity of a protected forest landscape.When should you plan a Dehradun wildlife trip?For those specifically hoping to see Tejas, it is worth waiting until the zoo officially announces that his quarantine period is over and that he is on public display. Travellers should check the latest zoo information.More than just a tiger sightingThe arrival of Tejas gives travellers another reason to revisit Dehradun, but the bigger story is the city's growing appeal as a base for nature, wildlife and outdoor experiences. From the Shivalik foothills and forested landscapes to nearby Rajaji and the road towards Mussoorie, Dehradun offers several ways to build a wildlife-and-nature-focused holiday.And once Tejas completes his quarantine, visitors may have an unusual opportunity: a white tiger in one enclosure and a more traditionally coloured Royal Bengal tiger nearby, offering a striking visual reminder of the natural variation found within the tiger species.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mercedes-Benz GLC EV India launch on this date: Details
articles.summary: Mercedes-Benz will launch the GLC Electric in India on November 4, 2026.
articles.body: Mercedes-Benz will launch the GLC Electric in India on November 4, 2026. The SUV will be assembled at the company’s Chakan plant in Pune and will arrive in the 400 4Matic version. Bookings are expected to open in October. Mercedes-Benz says the Indian launch will come just six months after the model went on sale in Europe, making it the fastest global model from the brand to be locally assembled in India.The GLC Electric 400 4Matic uses a 94kWh battery and has a claimed WLTP range of up to 715km. Its two electric motors power all four wheels and produce 490hp and 800Nm. Mercedes-Benz claims a 0-100kph time of 4.3 seconds, despite the SUV weighing around 2.5 tonnes.The electric SUV supports DC charging at up to 330kW. The company claims a 10-minute charge can add enough energy for up to 300km of range. The international-specification model also gets air suspension and rear-wheel steering with up to 4.5 degrees of steering angle.The GLC Electric gets a wide front grille with illuminated elements, projector LED headlights and star-shaped LED daytime running lights. Its design also includes flush door handles, wheel-arch cladding and alloy wheels of up to 21 inches.At the rear, the SUV gets star-shaped LED tail-lights with circular outlines, connected by a gloss-black strip. The front Mercedes logo is illuminated, while the rear gets a solid 3D badge. Internationally, the 400 4Matic can also be specified with an AMG Line package, which adds a different grille and sportier alloy wheels.The GLC Electric gets a 39.1-inch MBUX Hyperscreen, which Mercedes-Benz says is its largest car display. It combines the driver’s instrument screen, central infotainment display and passenger screen into one unit.The system runs on fourth-generation MBUX software and includes an AI assistant. The SUV also retains physical controls on the steering wheel and centre console, while seating is provided for five occupants.The Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric is expected to cost between Rs 80 lakh and Rs 90 lakh (ex-showroom). It will compete with the BMW iX3 Long Wheelbase, which is expected to launch in India in 2027.

articles.summary: GAYA: Smita Thackeray on Tuesday performed ‘pind daan’ and ‘shraddh’ rituals for her father-in-law and Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray, as well as
articles.body: GAYA: Smita Thackeray on Tuesday performed ‘pind daan’ and ‘shraddh’ rituals for her father-in-law and Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray, as well as her father Madhukar Chitre, at the Vishnupad Temple here.Accompanied by her ‘acharya’ (priest), Thackeray performed ‘tarpan’, puja and other rituals amid Vedic chants. She was later blessed by Mohan Lal Barik, the Thackeray family’s priest in Gaya.Speaking after the ceremony, Thackeray said she had come to Gaya to pray for peace for Balasaheb Thackeray’s soul and seek forgiveness for any mistakes she may have committed towards him.She said she would try to follow the path shown by Balasaheb and work towards carrying forward Sanatan Dharma and his idea of a Hindu Rashtra.Thackeray said she was initially told that women do not perform ‘pind daan’, following which she sought clarification from acharyas. According to her, the acharyas cited the religious account of Mata Sita performing ‘pind daan’ for King Dasharatha.According to religious belief, performing ‘shraddh’ and ‘pind daan’ in Gaya helps ancestors attain salvation.The ongoing Pitru Paksha fair has attracted large numbers of devotees from across India and abroad. articles.title: In 2018, Elon Musk donated $480,350 for Flint school water filters; four years later, redesigned systems allowed students to drink from fountains again after years of relying on alternative supplies
articles.summary: For four years, students at Flint Community Schools relied on bottled and delivered water instead of drinking directly from school fountains.
articles.body: For four years, students at Flint Community Schools relied on bottled and delivered water instead of drinking directly from school fountains. That is now changing after new ultraviolet water filtration systems were installed and tested across the district. The project dates back to 2018, when Elon Musk donated $480,350 to help install water filtration stations following the Flint water crisis. The upgraded systems are designed to remove lead, bacteria and other metals from water before it reaches students. District officials say testing found no detectable lead or harmful bacteria after filtration, allowing the drinking stations to be used again.How the new water filters workA total of 130 filtration stations have been installed across Flint's 11 schools and administration building.The systems use three stages of filtration. Water first passes through an activated carbon filter designed to remove lead, copper and other particles. It then goes through an ultrafilter to remove most bacteria. Finally, ultraviolet light is used to kill remaining bacteria and viruses.Testing found lead levels before filtration varied by school. The highest average was 219 parts per billion (ppb) at Accelerated Learning Academy, while one test at Scott Elementary recorded 620 ppb. The US Environmental Protection Agency's recommended action level is 15 ppb.After filtration, tests found no detectable lead or harmful bacteria at the tested sites.Why did the project take four yearsThe stations were installed during the 2019-20 school year, but researchers found problems with the original filters during testing. The systems produced inconsistent results and were not certified to meet National Sanitation Foundation standards.Researchers later redesigned the systems and began testing new units in 2021.Superintendent Kevelin Jones said students can now drink from the hydration stations, but the district will continue providing bottled water for the rest of the school year as some families may still have concerns.The district also plans regular testing and filter replacements to monitor water quality.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1988, a Malibu developer and his wife bought land for $1.7 million, built a 17,700-square-foot mansion in 1991, and decades later listed the estate for $90 million
articles.summary: Discover the luxury of Venezia Pacifica, a custom-built mansion in Malibu's Point Dume, listed at $90 million. This iconic estate has Hollywood history and Mediterranean architecture, offering unparalleled oceanfront views.
articles.body: The luxury real estate market is seeing the entry of the largest cliffside residential property on Malibu’s Point Dume with a staggering price tag of $90 million according to the Wall Street Journal.The 1.16-acre property, beyond its architectural grandeur, comes with pop culture status, having served as a backdrop for Hollywood movies and series including The O.C. and Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me.Historically known as Venezia Pacifica, the custom-built mansion was completed in 1991, following the couple's 1988 land purchase, and is being offered for sale for the first time by its original owners. Property records cited by the paper show the property was acquired in 1988 by the late real estate developer Ken Harges and his wife, Lorelei Harges, for $1.7 million. Since the passing of Ken Harges in 2016, and his wife later on, their daughters Bonnie Furgurson and Wendy Geweke have decided to list the multi-million-dollar asset due to immense logistical challenges required in managing an estate of this magnitude. The couple's daughters said their parents wanted to leave inland life for the California coastline.Mediterranean architecture and interior design The primary residence incorporates a floor plan which is strongly evocative of classic Italian architecture, and inspiration from the couple’s historical travels through Italy has been etched directly into its structure. This sentiment for the region was echoed by their daughters, who wrote in a joint email cited by the Wall Street Journal: "Our mother was proudly 100% Italian," they said, "and together my parents drew inspiration from their many travels throughout Italy.The exterior is defined by classic columns, a signature terracotta-tiled roof, and an expansive circular motor court centered around a custom water fountain. Embracing 176 feet of direct bluff frontage, the estate’s perimeter overlooks the Pacific. Outside, the ocean facing grounds are landscaped with gardens and a sunken pavilion with columns to frame views of the immediate coastline.Inside, the architectural centerpiece is a massive, two-story central ballroom consisting of a sweeping glass curtain wall and an overhead barrel-vaulted glass ceiling. This expansive area is symmetrically flanked by a formal dining room on one side and a private library on the other. While the entry area showcases an artistic staircase alongside a custom glass elevator enclosed in decorative wrought ironwork. Throughout the estate’s nine bedrooms, the designs include coffered ceilings, structural columns, and intricate decorative millwork. Additionally, the primary bedroom suite is fitted with dual walk-in closets featuring motorized clothing carousels. Set apart from the living quarters is a 9,500-square-foot subterranean garage that can provide parking for 20 vehicles.The dynamics of the real estate market The listing of the Malibu mansion is making its debut in a coastal submarket that is highly active. According to listing agent Chris Cortazzo of Compass, the broader volatility across the greater Los Angeles luxury housing sector has done little to dissuade the micro-market of Malibu, which continues to remain energetic.Ultimately, the extensive acreage's pricing draws precedent from a comparable oceanfront property located nearby at Little Dume Beach, which previously sold for $80 million.However, the caveat is that since Venezia Pacifica was constructed before California's coastal and building regulations and height limits grew stricter, replicating a compound of this specific scale and blufftop proximity would be difficult under current zoning parameters. This tension between regulation and property value is not unique to Malibu. A UCSB study found that properties within California’s regulated coastal zone were valued 18% to 25% higherthan comparable properties outside it. Researchers attribute the premium partly to regulations that protect ocean views and limit coastal development.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2000, a Colorado man gave up money to leave debt and financial motives behind; 12 years later, he was still surviving through foraging, gifts and discarded goods
articles.summary: Explore the intriguing story of Daniel Suelo, who abandoned money in 2000 to live a life of foraging and generosity for over a decade. Discover how his unique lifestyle challenges societal norms about money and self-sufficiency.
articles.body: Daniel Shellabarger, who later became known as Daniel Suelo, decided to live without money in autumn 2000 after leaving his last thirty dollars in a phone booth at a truck stop in Pennsylvania, according to an account by Clay Bonnyman Evans published in The Coloradan. Mark Sundeen’s book The Man Who Quit Money, published in 2012, gave an account of Suelo’s way of life in the vicinity of Moab, Utah, where Suelo lived in a cave and gathered wild foods, as well as collected leftover food. In a blog post reproduced by Peace Corps Online, Suelo described money as a stand-in for the past as debt and the future as credit, never the present. The man had led a moneyless life, which is different from total self-reliance, since Suelo would accept any freely donated gifts and rejected any money or bartering system. This article looks at Suelo's lifestyle alongside two other sources: a 2006 psychology study on money and a federal report on food waste.University of Colorado degree and Peace Corps service in EcuadorSuelo's background appeared ordinary. Peace Corps Online, in a document reprinted in 2009, listed Suelo as a former Peace Corps volunteer in Ecuador who had earned an anthropology degree at the University of Colorado and worked as a lab technician. Furthermore, it is mentioned that he was 48 years old and lived in a cave around one hour away from Moab. The Coloradan’s account, as preserved by Clay Bonnyman Evans, placed him in the class of 1984. The Deseret News reported that he had been depressed for about 10 years before his 2000 decision.Twelve years of foraging and scavenging, 2000 to 2012Sundeen’s version, as quoted in the blog Citydesert, depicts the 12 years of living without money in which Suelo lived on wild edibles, scavenged food, some roadkill and gifts. An Associated Press profile of Suelo, published in the Summit Daily in 2009, provides additional details. Suelo went through Moab's garbage once a week and found more than enough for himself. Suelo assured the reporter that he never got sick because of the scavenged food.He rejected barter because he saw it as a form of money, the Deseret News reported. In an interview on Becoming Minimalist, he disagreed with the intro calling him boastful for avoiding food stamps and any other government assistance since it might imply that he considers himself superior to those who need such help. Gordon Stevenson, who directed a film about Suelo, talked to AP about the contradiction between Suelo's way of life and his reliance on people who use money. The Coloradan reported in 2013 that he had lived in a cave outside Moab for 13 years. Peace Corps Online's account of his 2000 hitchhike shows he did not stay in one place. In a 2021 profile, Utah Stories reported that he had made a home near Moab during the 1990s, before he gave up money.Vohs, Mead and Goode's nine money experiments, 2006In The Psychological Consequences of Money, published in Science, Kathleen Vohs, Nicole Mead and Miranda Goode reported nine experiments. The 2006 experiments suggested that money primes a more self-reliant orientation, making people less dependent on others, which offers background on how life without money differs from ordinary financial life. Moreover, they preferred to engage in solitary play, solitary work, and sit themselves at a greater distance from an unfamiliar individual compared to people exposed to neutral terms.USDA food waste estimates for 2010: 133 billion pounds, 31 percentThe food recovered by Suelo fits into the national pattern, which is well-established. USDA's Economic Research Service published a paper titled "The Estimated Amount, Value, and Calories of Postharvest Food Losses at the Retail and Consumer Levels in the United States." According to the statistics provided there, 133 billion pounds, out of 430 billion pounds of food available for consumption, were wasted in 2010, which is 31% of the available food, retail value of which was estimated at $161.6 billion. According to the estimates provided by the agency, retailers wasted 43 billion pounds of food, which is 10% of the available amount, and consumers wasted 90 billion pounds, which is 21%. The amount of wasted calories amounted to 387 billion per day, and meat, poultry and fish accounted for 30% of the total value lost.The agency reported that there was an average loss of 1,249 calories per person per day. Meat, poultry, and fish constituted 30 percent of the food wasted in terms of value, amounting to $48 billion. Reasons for wastage at the retail level included broken equipment like malfunctioning cold storage, ordering more than required and discarding damaged produce. This is shown by Suelo’s experience of the visible effect of food wastage; however, there are many other kinds of wastage included in the above statistics that cannot be recovered from trash.Suelo's return to financial society, 2015 to 2021Utah Stories reported in 2021 that Suelo's moneyless period lasted about 15 years, from 2000 until he returned to financial society in 2015 to care for his parents. A 2021 profile by Utah Stories described him as living in Colorado with his mother. The profile also said that he was still adjusting to life in a money-based society after years without money.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2011, Gary Sinise launched his foundation to support military families; by November 2025, it had dedicated its 100th mortgage-free adapted smart home, giving wounded veteran Joe Bowser a new start
articles.summary: For nearly two decades, wounded Army veteran Joe Bowser had turned down an offer that could have made everyday life much easier for him.
articles.body: For nearly two decades, wounded Army veteran Joe Bowser had turned down an offer that could have made everyday life much easier for him. That changed in November 2025, when the Gary Sinise Foundation dedicated its 100th mortgage-free, specially adapted smart home to him. According to the Gary Sinise Foundation’s own 2025 year-end campaign page, the milestone home was built around Bowser’s mobility needs, giving him and his wife, Michele, a safer and more accessible place to live. The milestone marked a major moment in the foundation’s work to provide specially adapted homes for severely wounded veterans.The injury that changed Joe Bowser’s lifeBowser’s story goes back to his military service in Iraq. He had served in the Army and later returned to the reserves following the September 11 attacks. In 2004, he was deployed to Iraq, where a rocket attack in April that year left him with serious injuries to his right leg. Doctors initially tried to save the leg, but after several operations, amputation eventually became necessary. Adjusting to life after such a severe injury was not easy, but Bowser found a way to reconnect with something he enjoyed: ice hockey.He later took part in hockey programmes for veterans with service-related injuries. For Bowser, the sport offered more than a chance to play. It helped him regain a sense of normality and reconnect with an activity he enjoyed before his injury. It was in 2006 that he met Sinise, beginning a friendship that would continue for years.Why he kept saying no to a new homeThe offer of a specially adapted home did not immediately appeal to Bowser. In fact, he spent years turning it down. The Gary Sinise Foundation had considered Bowser for its R.I.S.E. programme, which provides custom-built homes for wounded veterans. In an interview with PEOPLE, Sinise said Bowser repeatedly suggested that another veteran should receive the opportunity instead. Sinise told PEOPLE that Bowser was among those veterans who did not necessarily believe their injuries were severe enough to warrant a specially built home. Eventually, however, Bowser agreed.The decision came as the limitations of his existing home became harder to ignore. His previous house in West Virginia was built in 1839 and had narrow hallways and doorways that were difficult to navigate in a wheelchair. The second floor had also become increasingly challenging and unsafe for Bowser. He sometimes uses a wheelchair when he cannot use his prosthetic leg, making the layout of the old house particularly difficult.A home built around the way he livesThe new Tennessee house was designed with those everyday challenges in mind. According to PEOPLE, the approximately 2,991-square-foot, three-bedroom, single-storey ranch near Fort Campbell was built so that Bowser could move throughout the home without having to deal with stairs. The design includes five-foot-wide hallways, lower cabinets that can be reached from a wheelchair and an accessible shower fitted with a heated bench. These may seem like small details, but for someone navigating a home with a prosthetic leg or wheelchair, they can change how easily everyday activities are managed.The idea behind the foundation's specially adapted homes is not simply to provide a veteran with a house. The homes are designed around the individual needs of the person who will live there, with accessibility and independence built into the design. For Bowser, that means being able to move around his home more easily and safely.A milestone for the Gary Sinise FoundationBowser’s house also marked an important moment for the Gary Sinise Foundation. The organisation dedicated its 100th mortgage-free adapted smart home to him in November 2025. Its campaign page describes the homes as specially designed for severely wounded veterans, with accessibility features intended to help recipients regain independence in their daily lives.The house also gives Bowser and Michele more room to spend time with their family. The couple have 10 grandchildren, and the new home provides a setting where family gatherings can happen without the accessibility barriers they faced in their previous house. For the foundation, reaching 100 homes represents more than a numerical milestone. Each project involves creating a home around the specific needs of a veteran whose life has been affected by a serious service-related injury.A friendship that became part of the storyBowser’s connection with Sinise has also become deeply personal over the years. According to PEOPLE, the two men became even closer after each experienced the loss of a son to cancer. Bowser’s son Justin died in November 2023, while Sinise’s son Mac died in January 2024. Sinise launched the Gary Sinise Foundation in 2011 to support service members, veterans, first responders and their families. His interest in supporting veterans was also influenced by his experience playing Lieutenant Dan in Forrest Gump and his desire to help veterans after their service.For Bowser, the new home provides a single-storey layout and accessibility features designed around his mobility needs, while giving him, Michele and their family more room to spend time together.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Save Democracy March' announced: INDIA bloc projects unity amid SIR row, targets PM Modi, Amit Shah
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced a series of nationwide protests against the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced a series of nationwide protests against the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, seeking to project opposition unity amid the ongoing row over voter rolls.Addressing a press conference after the INDIA bloc meeting, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the alliance would hold district-level “Save Democracy” marches and demonstrations outside district magistrate offices from October 2 to 8.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every district magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.He said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6. Kharge said the opposition had initially planned to hold the march on Wednesday but decided to organise it later with greater participation.“On October 6, all opposition MPs will march to the Election Commission. We wanted to go today itself, but we decided to call the MPs again and organise the protest properly, so we have fixed October 6 for the march,” he said.Kharge added that Rajya Sabha members and MPs from all parties, as well as those who wanted to “protect democracy in the country”, would be invited to join the march.The alliance also plans to seek an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu in the second week of October. Leaders of the opposition will submit a representation outlining what Kharge described as the difficulties they were facing and the constitutional issues involved.A fourth phase of the campaign will comprise five major rallies, with their dates and venues to be announced later.The INDIA bloc meeting also saw Kharge reiterate his criticism of the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He alleged that the poll panel was being influenced by the government and said the parties had agreed to fight the issue together.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every District Magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.Addressing the briefing, ex-Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee lashed out at the CEC and call on him to resign."He (CEC Gyanesh Kumar) must resign immediately. Let us save the democracy and make the security of the people, the voting rights... It is our constitutional rights. It is our obligation to the people. If people are not voting, if their voting are been looted and cheated, then where the country will go? So, our request... it our demand. Our forceful demand," the former Bengal CM said.The opposition has demanded a rollback of the SIR exercise, greater transparency in electoral rolls and safeguards against the exclusion of eligible voters. Kharge also called for the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls for future elections and sought prior notice, reasons and an effective appeal mechanism before legitimate voters are removed.The meeting was attended by representatives of Congress, SP, AITC, NCP(SP), SS (UBT), RJD, CPM, CPI, JKNC, JKPDP, JMM, CPI-ML, IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, RSP, KC(J) and AIFB.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Boeing to build US Navy’s sixth-gen F/A-XX fighter as India steps up its own plans
articles.summary: The US Navy has formally selected Boeing to build its next carrier-based fighter under the F/A-XX programme, ending a competition that had run for years
articles.body: The US Navy has formally selected Boeing to build its next carrier-based fighter under the F/A-XX programme, ending a competition that had run for years and putting the manufacturer back at the centre of America's future airpower plans. Boeing released a fresh render of the winning design alongside the announcement, offering the clearest look yet at what the Navy's sixth-generation jet is expected to look like, a tailless, sharply blended airframe built around all-aspect stealth shaping, reflecting the same design language now emerging across next-generation fighter programmes worldwide. Earlier last year, US President Donald Trump had unveiled the US Air Force's sixth-generation project, known as the F-47 at the Oval Office.That global race is exactly where India is now trying to find its footing. The defence ministry has confirmed that the country is simultaneously engaging with both of the world's leading sixth-generation fighter projects, the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) of the UK, Japan and Italy, and the Future Combat Air System (FCAS), now a largely French-led effort after Germany's exit. Defence minister Rajnath Singh has said India is planning to produce both fifth and sixth generation fighters domestically. FCAS, with France now firmly in the driving seat and Spain still on board, is expected to take its first flight around 2028-29, roughly coinciding with the planned first flight of India's own fifth-generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft, in a parallel timeline.The Franco-German split itself has worked in India's favour. Disagreements over aircraft carrier operability and nuclear delivery capabilities pushed Germany out of FCAS, but India, unlike Germany, already possesses both capabilities, making its operational doctrine a closer match for French requirements. The defence ministry told the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Defence earlier this month that it has initiated concerted efforts to co-join the French-led FCAS programme.The stakes behind this positioning are considerable. Sixth-generation fighters are expected to bring all-aspect stealth shaping, digital-first engineering, variable-cycle engines, gallium nitride-powered radars and directed-energy weapons, layered with artificial intelligence, cyber warfare tools and manned-unmanned teaming alongside loyal wingman drones. Boeing's F/A-XX win joins an increasingly crowded field, sitting alongside the US Air Force's F-47 under the Next Generation Air Dominance project, while China is already flight-testing its own J-36 and J-50 prototypes. For India, engaging both GCAP and FCAS is less about picking a side and more about ensuring it has a seat at the table as the rules of future aerial combat are being written.

articles.title: An Illinois woman allegedly concealed her mother’s body in a garage freezer for two years, assumed her identity and continued collecting Social Security and food benefits; prosecutors put the intended loss at $21,402
articles.summary: A Chicago case involving an elderly woman’s death has taken a new turn in federal court, with prosecutors alleging that her daughter concealed her
articles.body: A Chicago case involving an elderly woman’s death has taken a new turn in federal court, with prosecutors alleging that her daughter concealed her mother’s body in a garage freezer for nearly two years while continuing to collect government benefits in her name. According to the Chicago Tribune, Eva Bratcher, 72, has been indicted in U.S. District Court on two fraud counts tied to more than $20,000 in Social Security and food assistance benefits that prosecutors say were obtained after her mother’s death in 2021. The indictment was initially filed under seal in August and was announced Tuesday by the U.S. Department of Justice as part of a nationwide enforcement effort targeting Social Security fraud.Body allegedly kept in freezerThe report states that according to federal prosecutors, Bratcher’s 96-year-old mother, Regina Michalski, died on March 4, 2021, at the Chicago home the two women shared. Authorities allege that about a week later, Bratcher purchased a new freezer and placed her mother’s body inside it. Investigators later found the freezer receipt at the residence. The body remained undiscovered until January 2023, when a relative became suspicious and contacted Chicago police. An autopsy was subsequently conducted, although the results were inconclusive.The discovery triggered a separate criminal case in Cook County, where Bratcher was charged with concealing a death or moving a body and possessing a fraudulent identification document.Alleged identity theftThe report also states that the federal prosecutors now allege that the concealment was accompanied by a broader effort to continue accessing benefits intended for Michalski. The indictment alleges that Bratcher assumed her mother’s identity and continued receiving Social Security benefits after her death. Prosecutors also accuse her of using her mother’s Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits and an alternative Social Security number to obtain additional SNAP assistance for which she was allegedly not eligible. The intended loss in the federal case is listed at $21,402.Authorities also allege that Bratcher possessed at least one identification card bearing her mother’s name but Bratcher’s photograph when she was arrested in connection with the earlier case, the online report adds.Earlier case ended in guilty pleaThe federal charges follow a state prosecution stemming from the discovery of Michalski’s body. According to court records, Bratcher had recorded her mother’s death on a calendar at the home. She later pleaded guilty in August 2023 to concealing her mother’s death and received a sentence of 213 days in jail, with credit for time already served.Bratcher, a U.S. Army veteran who was born in Poland, also had previous convictions for forgery, violating an order of protection and domestic battery, according to court records. The new federal indictment focuses specifically on the alleged theft of government benefits and identity-related fraud rather than the concealment of the body itself.Federal fraud crackdownThe charges were announced as part of a broader Justice Department initiative focused on fraud involving Social Security programs. Federal authorities have increasingly targeted cases in which benefits continue to be collected after recipients die or are obtained through the use of another person's identity. Bratcher is scheduled to make her first appearance in federal court at the Dirksen U.S. Courthouse in Chicago. Court records did not list an attorney for her at the time the charges were announced. The federal indictment contains allegations, and Bratcher is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.Images Courtesy: Chicago Tribune and istockYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Gen Z needs to watch In the Mood for Love - a classic where intimacy is about grace & restraint
articles.summary: Su Li-zhen Chan (Maggie Cheug): I didn't think you'd fall in love with me. Chow Mo-wan (Tony Leung Chiu-wai): I didn't either.
articles.body: Su Li-zhen Chan (Maggie Cheug): I didn't think you'd fall in love with me. Chow Mo-wan (Tony Leung Chiu-wai): I didn't either. I was only curious to know how it started. Now I know. Feelings can creep up just like that. I thought I was in control.- In the Mood for LoveWhat if I told you the world’s best film on love is one where lovers barely touch each other? Their hands brush against one another in a couple of scenes. There are no kissing scenes or even scenes of passionate embrace. But once you watch In the Mood for Love, the 2000 masterpiece directed by Hong Kong-based Wong Kar Wai, your life will forever be changed.Love, desire, passion and relationships have all gone through a mammoth change in the 21st century. Cinema and popular culture have depicted almost all aspects of these tectonic changes; but every September 29—the day of the movie’s release in 2000—cine lovers worldwide watch In the Mood for Love yet again, and social media is abuzz as if the film had been released yesterday.Then there’s the fact that every prestigious poll on “greatest cinema” has the Wong Kar Wai classic on its top five list. Even now. The last poll was by The New York Times. In mid-2025, NYT published its milestone poll ranking the ‘100 Best Movies of the 21st Century’. Voted into the fourth position by a panel of film critics, directors and scholars was Wong Kar-wai’s masterpiece. It secured its place at the top tier of modern cinema. This high honour also builds upon decades of global critical acclaim.The film was previously placed second in the BBC’s 2016 poll of 21st-century cinema and claimed fifth place in the British Film Institute’s prestigious 2022 Sight & Sound critics' poll of the greatest films of all time. So what is it about a film where lovers just barely brush past one another that continues to draw in every generation? Even Gen X and Gen Alpha.Restraint, the invaluable currency in our hyper-connected worldWell, this film relies almost entirely on emotional restraint. To every generation first watching this film, it’s a revelation; but to this generation—so used to and exhausted with swiping right and left, and the inevitability of looking for love through an app—it hits different.We also live in an era dominated by high-budget spectacles, fast-paced editing and explicit screenwriting, and that’s what we often expect out of every love story on celluloid.In the Mood for Love does the opposite. It tells a story where the central lovers just pass one another on streets, think about each other—and their own all-encompassing loneliness—and have to keep up the pretence of being just next-door neighbours.Set in the crowded apartment blocks of 1962 Hong Kong, the narrative follows two neighbours: newspaper editor Chow Mo-wan (Tony Leung Chiu-wai) and corporate secretary Su Li-zhen (Maggie Cheung). Together, they make a painful discovery: their respective spouses are having an extramarital affair with each other.Rather than seeking sudden revenge or plunging into a physical affair of their own, Chow and Su draw close through shared grief. They role-play imaginary conversations to figure out how their partners betrayed them, while silently making a solemn promise to themselves: “We won’t be like them”. But they do fall in love with one another. And that promise hangs in the balance.The late legendary movie critic Roger Ebert had wrote about the film: "They are in the mood for love, but not in the time and place for it. They look at each other with big damp eyes of yearning and sweetness, and go home to sleep by themselves. Adultery has sullied their lives: his wife and her husband are having an affair. “For us to do the same thing,” they agree, “would mean we are no better than they are.” The key word there is “agree.” The fact is, they do not agree. It is simply that neither one has the courage to disagree, and time is passing..."Through this vow of self-control, Wong Kar-wai delivers a powerful and unforgettable emotional experience. His love is not an act of physical possession at all. It is a lingering, unfulfilled state of longing that stays in memory forever. It cuts you to pieces. Every scene. From the beginning till the end.For 21st-century audiences living in a hyper-connected world, this movie can feel like a meditation. Nothing in this movie is explicitly said or made obvious. Wong's vision of intimacy is this: true closeness is often born from what remains unsaid, untouched and unconsumed.The power of what is unsaid but lingers in the airTo understand Wong Kar-wai’s artistic genius, we must examine his definition of intimacy. In traditional romance movies, intimacy is usually shown through physical touch, explicit confessions or sexual union. Wong completely flips this formula.In his cinematic universe, physical contact is often brief or misleading, whereas true intimacy flourishes in shared spaces, quiet silences and mutual understanding.Reflecting on his storytelling approach, Wong explained the main direction he gave to actress Maggie Cheung during filming: “We’re not making a movie about what’s said – we’re making one about what’s hidden”.This idea forms the core of his aesthetic. Intimacy in In the Mood for Love is built through delicate body language, small gestures and the physical environment. Wong instructed his lead actors to let their hands do the talking, noting that hands betray what faces hide, and that desire lives in subtle details like holding a cigarette, holding a letter or touching the edge of a dress.This focus on small gestures is tied to the physical setting of 1960s Hong Kong. He recalled how tiny living spaces forced people together with no privacy. Life was an open book read over one’s shoulder, creating thick human connections inside buildings with paper-thin walls.In such a tight environment, romance could not be displayed openly without causing neighbourhood gossip and social shame. As a result, intimacy shifted into quiet daily routines, like, brushing past one another on narrow stairwells while carrying takeaway noodle tins, standing under rain-soaked awnings or waiting in dim hallways.Did the rice cooker change the definition of love?Wong pointed out that simple daily inventions like rice cookers, instant noodles and 24-hour convenience stores changed Asian intimacy far more deeply than romantic love letters, because these objects altered how people moved through space and met each other every day.For instance, when Chow and Su practise role-playing scenarios to understand their spouses' affair, they create a private emotional world. They pretend to confront each other, flirt and say goodbye. Yet, as they act out these scenes, the line between performance and reality begins to disappear. They fall in love by sharing the exact weight of their heartbreak. For instance, in a restaurant while having dinner, and both heartbroken by their spouses' betrayal, Chow orders Su's husband's favourite dish, and Su asks for Chow's wife's favourite. While biting into each piece both the protagonists are trying to process grief and trying to understand each other's spouses, who are having the affair. The scene is at once - jarring, uncomfortable, intimate and absolute heartbreak.Then of course, is Wong Kar-wai's brilliant choice of cinematography and music, which are main characters in this movie - as essential as the protagonists. Christopher Doyle, the cinematographer, and Yumeji's Theme, the main soundtrack of the film, composed by Shigeru Umebayashi.While In the Mood for Love takes place in 1962 and was released in 2000, its core themes continue to resonate with audiences today. Modern life is filled with rapid digital communication, dating apps, instant text messages and social media oversharing. Relationships can start quickly and end just as fast, with romance often reduced to quick interactions and immediate responses.Against this backdrop, the film’s slow unfolding feels striking. There is time to notice a glance, a pause, a hesitation. Feelings are allowed to exist without immediately being named or acted upon. The characters’ silences become as important as their conversations, and what they choose not to do becomes the most important part of the story.The film also leaves us with an intriguing idea about unfulfilled desire. What remains unresolved can acquire a strange permanence because it never has the opportunity to become ordinary. Chow and Su’s relationship remains suspended between possibility and impossibility – protected from the routines and compromises that might have accompanied another life together. That is why it continues to feel so intimate.The everlasting echo of unfulfilled desireThis turn-of-the-millennium movie is a major achievement in global cinema also because it captures a feeling that can transcend culture and age: the ache of wanting something that can never quite become yours.Its fourth-place spot on The New York Times list of the top 100 movies of the 21st century is only the latest recognition of a film that has remained remarkably alive in popular and critical culture.Through its rich colours, small physical gestures and expressive music, the film shows how much emotional weight can be carried by the smallest moments.That is the secret of its enduring appeal. In the Mood for Love does not give us the satisfaction of a conventional love story with a beginning, middle and resolution. It leaves us with a feeling — unfinished, unresolved and lingering. The romance ends, but the longing remains, suspended somewhere between memory and imagination.Maybe that’s why, more than two decades after its release, we keep returning to it.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2025, about a dozen Getty Villa workers stayed as the Palisades Fire reached the grounds, fighting spot fires and sealing galleries; the museum and ancient art survived untouched
articles.summary: In January 2025, Getty Villa employees bravely fought to save the museum's priceless Greek and Roman art from the devastating Palisades Fire, demonstrating the importance of preparation and emergency response in the face of natural disasters.
articles.body: Museums are designed to last for centuries, but a single windy afternoon can still endanger a collection. Ancient ceramics, bronze and marble have survived graves, wars and earthquakes, and once they are lost, they cannot be restored. That was the risk facing the Getty Villa, a Pacific Palisades museum of Greek and Roman art, when a brush fire was reported about two miles away on January 7, 2025.It turned out that a combination of astute engineering and courageous individuals was the solution. According to Getty, every employee except about a dozen security and facilities volunteers went home. Those who stayed worked from the Villa's Emergency Operations Center, sealed the museum doors and put out small fires around the grounds while the main fire burnt nearby.When the smoke cleared, the buildings of the Villa were unharmed, and the art inside was undamaged, although the grounds did lose a considerable number of trees. This is not a call for ordinary people to stay put when told to evacuate. The Villa appears to have benefited from a detailed emergency plan, a purpose-built site and a direct line to fire authorities. Their experience offers lessons on preparation.A museum built for fireThe Villa had been built with fire in mind long before that January day. Getty says its walls are reinforced concrete beneath a tiled roof, and fire-rated doors can prevent smoke or flames from spreading to the rest of the site. A carbon-filtered air conditioner maintains a steady flow of pressure, which can be increased to keep out smoke and ash. In each room, detectors are set to an extremely low threshold to detect a fire at its earliest stage.The sprinklers are a surprise. They are kept absolutely dry to avoid accidental water damage and are only used as a last option. In case of loss of the main utility pressure, a backup water reservoir will serve the site. Emergency generators will operate the fire systems and lighting for weeks.Outside, the gardens had been constructed with fire in mind. The property is surrounded by oak trees, which absorb water effectively and burn more slowly than other plants; an irrigation system keeps the soil moist; and grounds staff clear low brush throughout the year, working beyond the distance the Los Angeles Fire Department requires.Timing also helped: the Villa was closed to the public on Tuesdays, so no visitors were on site when the fire arrived. Getty’s emergency preparedness specialist, Les Borsay, was testing the fire alarm system around 10 a.m. on Jan. 7 when a phone warning came in reporting a brush fire about two miles away. Within two hours, he said, it was already quite near. But buildings don’t put out a fire on a lawn, and that’s where the crew came in.Inside the long dayThe scale of the fire explains why the Villa could not count on outside help. CAL FIRE said the Palisades Fire began at 10:30 a.m. on Jan. 7, 2025, burned 23,448 acres before it was fully contained on Jan. 31, destroyed 6,845 structures, damaged 975 others and killed 12 civilians. As the fire spread, thousands of structures were in its path, and crews could not be committed to any one siteWithin the Villa the volunteers got themselves organised. The engineering manager monitored the humidity levels in the galleries and took action when alarms sounded, switching building systems to safeguard the collection and sealing the museum doors. The teams at the Villa and at the Getty Center in Brentwood checked security cameras for signs of flames, and the Center's personnel assisted in sending warnings when some radios at the Villa stopped working. Others patrolled in security vehicles, keeping watch on weak spots such as a parking area where cars would have been dangerous if they caught fire.Staff took turns during the day and into the night to step into the hot, smoky air and put out tiny flames with extinguishers, shovels or their boots. They put on N95 masks and goggles and were warned to return indoors after 20 to 30 minutes. Fires broke out in rosemary vines near the visitor car park, in plants above the Outdoor Classical Theatre, and immediately outside the front gate.“The difficulty was the wind; as soon as one fire was extinguished, another popped up behind them,” said security supervisor Carl Gordon. “My crew used at least 40 five-pound extinguishers.” None of them were firefighters. “I was at the Villa for 28 hours straight,” adds Borsay. Others stayed for 72 hours, sleeping in turns. Flames were near. The team dialled 911 to direct firemen to adjacent fires. Water was dropped by air on a slope near to the Ranch House, the first Getty museum, and firefighters were welcome to fill their vehicles from the Villa’s 50,000-gallon water tank.What other museums can learnUS Forest Service scientist Jack Cohen's research suggests that whether a home ignites during an extreme wildfire is largely determined by the house and its surroundings within about 100 feet, with flying embers and small surface fires among the main threats. That is consistent with the villa's practice of cutting brush early and keeping the soil damp. It also suggests why putting out small fires promptly can make a difference.The Getty team has been candid about what did not go so well. "The modest five- and 10-pound extinguishers we used were never intended for brush fires," Borsay told ABC7. Getty staff have since told other cultural institutions that water-based extinguishers work better than dry chemical ones in strong wind, and that staff should be sent home early.There was also the human side. Gordon said family members continued asking him why he had not left. After 30 years at the Villa, he said he felt a sense of responsibility for the institution. Security staff also handed out food, drink and torches to stranded neighbours nearby.About a dozen volunteers stayed at the Villa, but they did so under a plan, with training and with fire services close at hand. For everyone else, the official advice remains the same: when evacuation orders are issued, leave. Let preparation done ahead of time do the work.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2025, two brothers stayed through California’s Eaton Fire to protect their parents’ 65-year-old home; they saved it and, their family says, helped save nearby homes too
articles.summary: In a heroic act during California's Eaton Fire, brothers Justin and his sibling defended their family's 65-year-old home, saving it and potentially nearby houses from destruction. Follow their courageous journey as they battle the flames to protect their mother's legacy.
articles.body: Justin Murphy had gotten his 93-year-old mother, Jane, out of their Altadena home when the Eaton Fire began bearing down on the neighborhood in the early hours of Jan. 8, 2025, following which he went back to the house with his brother. The two spent the night using hoses and sprinklers to fight the fire and protect the property, which their parents had bought 65 years earlier. The main home survived, although a detached garage and study were destroyed, KQED reported in March 2025.The Murphy home stood on a secluded cul-de-sac in northeast Altadena with views toward the San Gabriel Mountains, and KQED reported that eight homes had stood on the street for more than a century. Only two houses remained by the time Murphy returned weeks after the fire: his mother's house and a neighbor's home across the street, while the rest had burned.The Eaton Fire began on Jan. 7 near Altadena and Pasadena, and CAL FIRE records show that the blaze eventually burned 14,021 acres and destroyed more than 9,000 structures. It was declared contained on Jan. 31 after 24 days. The immediate problem for the Murphys was to keep the flames from taking hold of the property. Justin and his brother worked through the night as embers and fire moved through the neighborhood, after they made sure that their mother was safe before returning to defend the house.The house was not the only thing they were trying to protectJane Murphy later told KQED that she believed her sons' actions may have protected other homes on the street as well, with her reasoning being that if the Murphy house and the neighboring property had both caught fire, the flames could have spread to other homes farther downwind. Justin later told KQED that he believed that their actions prevented the fire from gaining a foothold in the house. He created a text chain that provided updates to more than a dozen people who had left the area. There were checkpoints that restricted access to Altadena after the fire, and those updates became one way for residents outside the neighborhood to learn what was happening around their homes.Los Angeles County's recovery records now describe the Eaton Fire as a massive wildfire that consumed more than 14,000 acres and destroyed more than 9,000 structures in Altadena. The county continues to operate recovery programs for residents whose homes and properties were damaged or destroyed.The fire moved through Altadena under extreme conditionsThe Eaton Fire started at about 6:18 p.m. on Jan. 7, according to the final CAL FIRE record, and the agency lists the cause as electrical. On Jan. 8, the record described strong winds, low humidity and dry fuels that were contributing to rapid fire growth and spot fires. The agency reported that firefighters were working to protect critical infrastructure while multiple structures were already being damaged or destroyed.Los Angeles County reported that the Eaton Fire had burned 14,021 acres by Jan. 24, with 9,418 structures destroyed and 1,073 damaged, but those numbers were still subject to verification as damage inspections continued. The Murphy house was among the small number of properties that remained standing on its street. The garage and study were gone, but the main residence was still usable.Returning to a neighborhood that had changedJustin remained in Altadena after the immediate danger passed while much of the neighborhood was still under restrictions. KQED reported that military-enforced security checkpoints prevented many people from returning for roughly two weeks. Murphy was detained several times while moving around the area, but if he left through a checkpoint, it could mean losing the ability to return.His mother eventually went back to the house once the checkpoints were lifted, and KQED reported that she resumed her regular two-mile walks through the neighborhood even as burned properties surrounded her. The family's house was still standing, but the street around it had been transformed; it had once been eight homes but was reduced to two. The Eaton Fire's wider recovery has continued through rebuilding programs, debris removal, infrastructure work and assistance for residents across Altadena. Los Angeles County maintains a dedicated recovery portal for the community. The property the Murphy family bought 65 years earlier survived the fire with part of the house intact, but the detached garage and study were lost, while most of the surrounding homes were destroyed.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Michigan woman entrusted with managing Social Security benefits for her elderly disabled uncle allegedly took nearly $121,000 over seven years while prosecutors say he lived without running water, electricity or heat
articles.summary: A case from Michigan is among several Social Security fraud cases announced by the US Department of Justice as part of a nationwide enforcement effort
articles.body: A case from Michigan is among several Social Security fraud cases announced by the US Department of Justice as part of a nationwide enforcement effort targeting the misuse of federal benefits. According to the US Department of Justice (DOJ), Laura Whisenant allegedly misused nearly $121,000 in Social Security benefits belonging to her elderly, mentally disabled uncle over a period of seven years. The DOJ says Whisenant was serving as his representative payee, a role that allowed her to manage the benefits on his behalf. Prosecutors allege that while the money was being misused, her uncle was living in extremely poor conditions, in a house without running water, electricity or heat. The allegations form part of a broader September 2026 DOJ announcement detailing criminal cases involving more than $1.3 million in intended losses to the US government. Whisenant has been charged under federal law concerning the misuse of Social Security benefits. Because the case is based on a complaint, the allegations against her have not been proven in court.She was responsible for managing her uncle’s benefitsWhisenant's role in the case is significant because she was not simply accused of accessing someone else's Social Security payments. According to the DOJ, she had been appointed as the representative payee for her elderly, mentally disabled uncle. A representative payee is responsible for receiving and managing Social Security benefits for someone who is unable to manage those benefits independently. The money is meant to be used for the beneficiary's needs.According to the DOJ complaint, Whisenant allegedly used that position to take and misuse nearly $121,000 in her uncle's Social Security benefits over seven years. The department lists the intended loss associated with the case as $121,980. The allegation covers a considerable period, meaning the purported misuse was not described as a single withdrawal or isolated incident. Prosecutors say the benefits were misused over seven years while Whisenant was serving in the representative-payee role.Prosecutors say her uncle was living without basic utilitiesThe circumstances surrounding the alleged misuse are a central part of the case. According to the DOJ, Whisenant's uncle was living in a house without running water, electricity or heat while she allegedly misused his benefits. The department described him as elderly and mentally disabled. That detail is particularly important because representative payees are entrusted with managing benefits for people who may need assistance handling their own finances. The money is intended to support the beneficiary rather than serve as a source of personal funds for the person managing it.The case was part of a wider Social Security fraud crackdownWhisenant's case was announced alongside several other federal cases involving alleged theft or misuse of Social Security benefits. The Justice Department said its National Fraud Enforcement Division, working with US Attorneys' Offices in 11 districts and the Social Security Administration's Office of Inspector General, brought charges against 17 defendants between August 21 and September 18. The department said those defendants were allegedly responsible for more than $1.3 million in intended losses to the United States. The cases involved different types of alleged conduct.In one case from Illinois, prosecutors accused a woman of concealing her deceased mother's body in a freezer while allegedly continuing to collect her mother's Social Security and other benefits. Another defendant in New York was accused of continuing to withdraw money from his deceased brother's account after his death while Social Security payments continued to be deposited. Other cases involved people who allegedly acted as representative payees for relatives or children receiving benefits. The DOJ said the cases were part of a broader effort to identify and prosecute fraud involving Social Security Administration benefit programmes, including Supplemental Security Income.What happens next in the Michigan caseThe federal charge against Whisenant concerns 42 U.S.C. § 408(a)(5), a provision relating to fraud, misrepresentation or misuse involving Social Security benefits. The DOJ lists a maximum penalty of five years in prison for the charge. That maximum penalty does not mean that a particular sentence will be imposed. The outcome of a criminal case depends on the court proceedings, evidence, applicable sentencing rules and other factors. For now, the allegations remain allegations. The DOJ's announcement identifies the case as a complaint, rather than announcing a conviction or sentence. The case also highlights the responsibility that comes with managing government benefits for someone who cannot manage them independently. In this instance, prosecutors allege that nearly $121,000 in benefits were misused over seven years while the elderly beneficiary lived without basic household utilities.The broader DOJ enforcement action shows that representative-payee arrangements are one of several areas being examined as federal authorities pursue alleged Social Security fraud. For Whisenant, the next stage will be the federal court process, where the allegations outlined by prosecutors can be tested against the evidence and a final legal determination can be made.You use AI every day.
